clue.text: Scholar presenting display to queen

parts.note: an exhibition is a public display
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: A student shows off a project in front of the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: An exhibitioner is a student holding an exhibition, a kind of scholarship at a British university or school.
explanation.definitionFit: An exhibitioner holds a scholarship award called an exhibition, so is a type of scholarship student.

clue.text: A number rising without tea to keep fast

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so these letters go around the next piece
in a down clue, rising means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: nine is a number
cha is an informal word for tea

explanation.surface: A count of something climbs while the tea runs out, and someone tries to hold on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking, and 'rising' suits a down clue read from the bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchain is to bind in chains, to hold someone fast and stop them escaping.

clue.text: One detesting being around married son's pet

indicators.note: the first piece sits around the following letters

parts.note: someone who detests is a hater
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone who loathes animals is stuck with the newlywed couple's boy's little pet.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamster is a small rodent commonly kept as a household pet.

clue.text: Fish from Scottish island caught outside of unfished area

parts.note: Barra is an island in the Outer Hebrides of Scotland
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A catch is landed off a Hebridean island, just beyond waters nobody has fished.
explanation.definitionFit: The barracuda is a predatory sea fish with long sharp teeth.

clue.text: The flower of Rome finds tribe giving resistance to the last

indicators.note: the named letter is shifted to the final position of the word it came from

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Rome's finest people show that a clan fought on until the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is the crossword trick for something that flows, a river; R in TRIBE moves 'to the last', giving TIBE + R.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tiber is the river that runs through Rome, and a flower in crosswords is a river.

clue.text: As it turns out, prove to surpass

indicators.note: turns out suggests the letters being turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Events show that somebody has managed to outdo the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtop is to rise above or exceed, the same as to surpass.

clue.text: Hartnell creation lacking line to captivate

indicators.note: a creation is something newly made, so the letters are formed into something new
the rearranged letters must go without the following piece

explanation.surface: A Hartnell gown, missing one line of its design, still manages to charm.
explanation.walkthrough: Norman Hartnell was the Queen's couturier, hence 'creation' as a dress; the letters of HARTNELL less one L ('lacking line') rearrange into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To enthral is to hold someone spellbound, which is to captivate them.

clue.text: Singer's failure to hit note, left with throat condition

definitions.note: the definition 'Singer' plus 's, meaning 'is', linking it to the wordplay

parts.note: a miss is a failure to hit
E is one of the musical notes
thrush is a fungal infection of the mouth and throat

explanation.surface: A vocalist cracks on a note and is left with a sore throat.
explanation.definitionFit: The mistle or missel thrush is a songbird, so a singer in crossword terms.

clue.text: Immigrant in Norfolk resort? That's not right

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: not right says R, the abbreviation for right, is removed

parts.note: Cromer is a seaside resort in the English county of Norfolk

explanation.surface: Someone from abroad turns up in an English seaside town, and a local objects.
explanation.definitionFit: An incomer is someone who has newly arrived to live in a place, an immigrant.

clue.text: During swim, Royal Engineers use aqualungs, perhaps

indicators.note: the next piece happens within the first, so it goes inside it

parts.note: to bathe is to go for a swim
RE is the abbreviation for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Army engineers take a dip with diving gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Divers use aqualungs in order to draw air, so using one is an example of drawing breath.

clue.text: Former fairy distressed in tale learnt from life

parts.note: ex means former
a peri is a fairy or sprite in Persian mythology

indicators.note: distressed means damaged or roughed up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A one-time fairy is upset in a story that draws on real life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distressed' rearranges IN and TALE into ENTIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Experiential means derived from experience, so knowledge gained by living.

clue.text: Hindu sacred writings partly showed Ganesh as traitor

indicators.note: only a part of these words is used, a run hidden across them

explanation.surface: Religious texts portray the elephant god Ganesh as a betrayer.
explanation.definitionFit: A shastra is a Hindu treatise or body of sacred scripture.

clue.text: Role sailor rejected as' rodent catcher

indicators.note: rejected suggests turned back, so each piece is read backwards

parts.note: a part is a role in a play
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor turns down a part as a rodent catcher.
explanation.walkthrough: One indicator, 'rejected', turns each piece where it stands; the stray apostrophe after 'as' is a printing slip.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattrap is a device for catching rats, which are rodents.

clue.text: Be reluctant to go on grand departing ship

indicators.note: departing says the following letter leaves the word

parts.note: to linger is to stay on, reluctant to leave
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: Someone hangs back about leaving on a great voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: A liner is a large passenger ship sailing a regular route.

clue.text: Not in and out of love?

definitions.text: Not in and out of love?

parts.words: Not in and out of love?
parts.note: 'not in' means unfashionable, out of favour; read the other way, someone no longer loved by people is out of their affection

explanation.walkthrough: 'In' as fashionable and 'out of love' as no longer liked both describe a person or thing nobody cares for.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disliked or out of favour is no longer in fashion and no longer loved by the public.

clue.text: Like some secretaries entrap men all over the place

indicators.note: scattered everywhere, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Office secretaries scheme to ensnare men in every corner.
explanation.walkthrough: A permanent secretary is the senior civil servant running a British government department.
explanation.definitionFit: Permanent secretaries head UK ministries, so permanent describes some secretaries.

clue.text: Good stuffing — chestnut, perhaps with hot characteristic

parts.note: a chestnut is a horse of reddish-brown colour
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
an air is a characteristic manner or quality

explanation.surface: A chestnut stuffing recipe with a fiery quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chestnut' invites the nut in a stuffing; it is a horse colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Horsehair was traditionally used as quality padding in upholstered furniture and mattresses.

clue.text: Is fragrant oil served after right Italian dish?

indicators.note: the following pieces come after the letter for right

parts.note: taken as written
otto, or attar, is a fragrant oil from rose petals

explanation.surface: A diner asks whether a perfumed oil is served with the right Italian meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian rice dish cooked slowly in stock.

clue.text: Hartley novel is mundane

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A book by L. P. Hartley is ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthly means belonging to this world rather than heaven, as mundane does.

clue.text: Piece musician comes in regularly to perform?

definitions.text: Piece musician comes in regularly to perform?

parts.words: Piece musician comes in regularly to perform?
parts.note: a musical composition in which each voice or player joins at set intervals with the same theme

explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' looks like an instruction to take alternate letters, but no run gives the answer: the clue describes how the parts enter one after another in this form.
explanation.definitionFit: In this contrapuntal form a subject is stated by each voice in turn, entering in succession.

clue.text: Goddess offering lots as the price of fish

parts.note: for means in exchange for, as in sold for a sum
tuna is a fish

explanation.surface: A deity hands out a fortune for the cost of some fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortuna was the Roman goddess of luck, who handed out fortunes and lots.

clue.text: Farewell run at cricket that's not bad?

parts.note: good means not bad
a bye is a run scored in cricket from a ball the batsman did not hit

explanation.surface: A parting word for an extra run on the cricket pitch, not a bad one.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodbye is the usual word said when parting, a farewell.

clue.text: University private secretary's to strongly advocate a rise

parts.note: PS is the abbreviation for private secretary
to urge is to advocate strongly

explanation.surface: A college secretary pushes hard for a pay increase.
explanation.definitionFit: An upsurge is a sudden increase, so a rise in something.

clue.text: Chips without fish? Come on

indicators.note: without means the next piece is removed

parts.note: Chips is the traditional nickname for a ship's carpenter
a carp is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Someone offering fries but no fish is told to come along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chips without fish' suggests a takeaway order; Chips is a carpenter's nickname, and 'Come on' is stage language for appearing.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter is to come on, as an actor comes on stage.

clue.text: Just missing flight at first, then left here?

definitions.text: Just missing flight at first, then left here?

indicators.note: the following letter goes missing from the first word

parts.note: fair means just

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A traveller narrowly misses a plane and has to stay put.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the place: you have just missed your flight and are left there.
explanation.definitionFit: The place where a missed flight leaves a passenger stranded is the terminal and runway complex for planes.

clue.text: Cutter emerged, but finally lost time

indicators.note: the last letter is lost and the next piece takes its place

parts.note: chicks emerge from the egg when they are hatched

explanation.surface: The chicks came out, but at the end time ran out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally lost' drops the final D of HATCHED; T for 'time' takes its place.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatchet is a small axe, a tool for cutting.

clue.text: Outer city area seen returning across border between Douai- Bruxelles?.

indicators.note: returning means those letters are read backwards
seen means visible within, so the letters lie in the words that follow

explanation.surface: A suburban district is spotted on the way back over the frontier between French and Belgian cities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across border between' points to the run spanning the end of Douai and the start of Bruxelles; 'returning' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Exurbia is the prosperous zone of settlements beyond the suburbs of a city.

clue.text: Your elephant running for compound

indicators.note: running suggests the letters are on the move into a new order

explanation.surface: An elephant belonging to you is on the loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Polyurethane is a synthetic polymer, a chemical compound used for foams and varnishes.
